candidates.exact_span: in order for a permittee to be in compliance with the Forum's municipal discharges criteria, the incremental increase in salinity shall be 400 mg/L or less, which is considered to be a reasonable incremental increase above the flow weighted average salinity of the intake water supply.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes the default enforceable numeric TDS/salinity incremental-increase limit (400 mg/L above flow-weighted intake salinity). A different reading of this criterion or its intake-baseline methodology would change which numeric limit is applied when comparing reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: However, the permitting authority may permit a discharge in excess of the 400 mg/L incremental increase at the time of issuance or reissuance of a NPDES discharge permit, upon satisfactory demonstration by the permittee that it is not practicable to attain the 400 mg/L limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Provides an alternative-limit pathway when practicability cannot be demonstrated. Whether this exception applies (and what substitute limit it authorizes) would change the enforceable numeric limit used for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: April 10, 2015, the facility demonstrated that it was economically impractical to attain the net 400 mg/L incremental increase limit at that time. Because of that demonstration, EPA allowed a temporary 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit of 497 mg/L for the previous permit cycle, provided that the facility will diligently control and reduce TDS in their discharge (i.e., maintaining the formulated BMP activities, monitoring its effluent quality and quantity on a regular basis, and completing $14 million upgrades at the WWTP to improve overall effluent quality (i.e., reducing TDS in their discharges)).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies a facility-specific temporary 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit (497 mg/L) and associated conditions (BMP maintenance, regular effluent monitoring, upgrade completion). Interpretation of whether this temporary limit, its averaging period, or its conditions carry into FY2025 would change applicable numeric limits (A), whether effluent monitoring was required (B), and how missing or conditional monitoring evidence is classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: The City of Farmington has constructed a new sampling station where water intake samplings have been conducted.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Intake sampling is needed to compute the flow-weighted intake salinity baseline for net incremental increase limits. Whether intake monitoring was required and whether available intake data support limit derivation would change both the applicable limit calculation (A) and monitoring-obligation determinations (B).

candidates.exact_span: EPA believes the TDS data collected during the past permit cycle are sufficient and representative of facility existing operation conditions and can be used to derive the final 30-day average net incremental increase limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Agency conclusion that prior-cycle TDS data are sufficient to derive the final limit affects which numeric limit is established (A) and how periods without ordinary reported results or with reliance on historical data are characterized when evidence is incomplete (C).

candidates.exact_span: EPA cannot grant the permittee request of keeping the temporary 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit of 497 mg/L in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Explicitly rejects continuation of the 497 mg/L limit in the draft permit, implying a different enforceable 30-day average net incremental increase limit applies for the new permit term. This directly changes which numeric limit is used for exceedance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: To protect and maintain existing water quality as required by 40 CFR §122(4)(d) and to prevent further degradation of water quality in the San Juan River in accordance with 40 CFR §131.12, Subsection A of 20.6.4.8 NMAC, the New Mexico Continuing Planning Process –
candidates.computation_change_reason: States the regulatory basis for setting a limit other than the requested 497 mg/L. Interpretation of these anti-degradation and planning-process requirements could affect which final numeric limit EPA derives, even though the segment truncates before stating the resulting limit value.
